title: Toorow Source Capabilities
description: Canonical contract for connector report capabilities and their scoped public representation.

label_source_field.description: Epic 31: for kind='event' only -- the provider source field carrying the human LABEL of the event instance (level 3 of platform>type>label). Null/absent for metric/dimension fields. An event field sets aggregation='none', non_additive=false (both N/A for a temporal marker).

derivation.description: CALCULATED/DERIVED metric (kind='metric' only). The metric EXISTS in the provider API (declared here for catalogue completeness) but its provider-computed value is NOT trusted as an additive fact -- it is RECONSTRUCTED downstream from additive components. Implies non_additive=true. 'imported' selects the flavour: false (default) = provider value DROPPED at import and recomputed from components; true = provider value ALSO landed raw as a non-additive column for parity/audit, never summed. Declaring the reconstruction here lets the semantic/mart layer generate it instead of hardcoding it per connector.

scale.description: multiplier applied after division: 1000 for eCPM/CPM (per mille), 100 for a percentage, 1/absent otherwise

expression.description: free-form recomputation over canonical fields (method='expression'), e.g. 'clicks / impressions'

imported.description: false (default) = provider value dropped at import and reconstructed downstream; true = also landed raw as a non-additive column for parity, never summed

money.description: Story 39.2: money adapter INPUT contract (kind='metric' monetary field). Declares the connector's NATIVE money encoding. The platform adapter (server/core/money.py) normalizes this to the ONE canonical internal unit = micros, currency attached (E39-AD1); the /1e6 division back to display units happens ONCE at read. Absent => not a monetary field (39.1's monetary classification is the governed set; this adds the orthogonal native-encoding axis). ADDITIVE / backward-compatible: absent = today's behaviour.

currency_source.description: Opaque locus of the source currency (e.g. a field id or 'network'); the ADAPTER reads it, core never names a provider (AD-2).

display_name.description: The connector's own name for this report (report_profiles[].display_name). Null when the manifest does not name it; the console then falls back to the id.

description.description: What this report answers, in the connector's words. Null when unstated.

max_provider_backfill_days.description: How many days back THIS report may be re-collected from the provider, as the provider's own documentation states it -- a hard reporting window (e.g. Search Console's 16 months), never a customer-configurable retention setting and never an estimate. Read by core.datastream_source_catalogue._declared_backfill_bound (which looks it up HERE, in source_capabilities.reports -- `_connector_option_contract` drops it, so this is the only place it can live) and published to the Workbench through datastream_dimension_history as `earliest_recoverable`. Declared in this schema on 2026-08-17. Until then the key was not merely unused: `additionalProperties: false` on this object made it INVALID, so the measured '0 of 140 reports declare it' was a schema refusal, not an oversight -- every report published `None` and no manifest could have said otherwise. ABSENT REMAINS A VALID ANSWER: it means the provider publishes no hard bound, and the module then owes a manifest-level `_max_provider_backfill_days_note` saying so (test_backfill_bound_is_declared_or_its_absence_is). A bound is never guessed -- 0 and false are refused by the reader, and a wrong number promises a history the provider never committed to.

date_axis.description: How this report carries the date. 'request_dimension': the source accepts the day beside the report's other dimensions, so one request covers the window and the day is read from the answer. 'per_day_request': the source refuses that combination, so the daily grain is obtained one request per day and the day is stamped from the window. Absent = 'request_dimension'. Which one applies is the SOURCE's answer, measured against it, never a rule applied to every report of a connector.

_date_axis_note.description: What the source answered, and when it was measured.

entity_field.description: The field_id of source_capabilities.fields[] that identifies WHAT each row of this bundle is about -- the entity identifier. Declared on an event bundle (landing 'context_events'), whose pull carries it to app.context_events.entity_key. `_normalize_report` then carries it among this report's `dimensions`, which is what makes it mappable, pinnable and a candidate component of an MDM common key (datastream-workbench-and-wizard.md, amendment 2026-09-06). Absent means the bundle's rows are about no particular entity -- a holiday, a price change -- and nothing is added.

entity_kind.description: What `entity_field` identifies, in the connector's own words ('video', 'product', 'campaign') -- the exact value the pull writes to app.context_events.entity_kind, so the declaration and the row agree. Meaningless without `entity_field`.

landing.description: Epic 31: where this profile's pull lands. Absent = derived at load (module_kind=='context' -> context_events, else fact_daily_kpi). A connector may mix landings across profiles (e.g. YouTube kpi profiles + a video_upload event profile), so 'landing' -- not module_kind -- decides the write path and the conformance layer.

events.description: Epic 31: for a landing='context_events' profile -- the kind='event' field ids this profile emits (metrics/dimensions stay empty). A kpi profile leaves this empty/absent.

time_context.description: Story 39.7: report-timezone CAPTURE contract INPUT (DESCRIPTOR level -- one report timezone per datastream/network/property, contrast 39.2's per-field money). Declares WHERE this connector reads the exact report timezone the source used to draw its reporting-day boundaries, and its fallback posture when it cannot be determined. The platform (server/core/report_timezone.py) validates the captured IANA zone and, when absent, emits a typed TIMEZONE_GAP or records the declared assumption as TAGGED provenance -- NEVER a silent UTC/default (E39-NFR02). Source-agnostic: 'locus' names an ABSTRACT source of the zone, never a provider field (AD-2). Absent => connector captures no report timezone yet (treated as locus='none': a TIMEZONE_GAP for its date-grain figures). ADDITIVE / backward-compatible.

locus.description: Abstract source of the report timezone: 'network'/'property'/'account' = read from provider metadata at pull; 'fixed' = the provider always reports in one declared zone (see fixed_zone); 'none' = the provider exposes no report timezone (=> TIMEZONE_GAP).

fallback.description: Posture when the zone cannot be determined at pull: 'gap' = refuse to assume, surface TIMEZONE_GAP (fail-closed, the default posture); 'assume' = record an explicitly-declared assumed_zone as a TAGGED assumption in provenance (never silent) -- requires assumed_zone.

fixed_zone.description: IANA zone when locus='fixed' (the one zone the provider always reports in). Null otherwise.

assumed_zone.description: IANA zone recorded as a TAGGED assumption when fallback='assume' and the live zone is undetermined. Null when fallback='gap'.

report_timezone_lever.description: Story 39.8: declares whether THIS source exposes a report-timezone setting in its dimension filters (RARE). Present => the user can change the reporting timezone at the source, and the cross-source day-offset SIGNAL points them there; absent/null => the timezone is fixed on the detected value (no lever) and the datastream is reported as 'fixed on the detected timezone, no lever available'. This is the ADJUSTMENT-LEVER axis, orthogonal to time_context's CAPTURE axis (39.7). GAM has no lever (its timezone is a fixed NETWORK property, not a report filter) => it declares nothing here (has_lever:false). Core NEVER names a provider (AD-2): the connector declares the lever locus OPAQUELY, surfaced verbatim to the user as lever_hint, never interpreted by core. ADDITIVE / backward-compatible: absent = today's behaviour (no lever).

locus.description: Opaque hint WHERE the report-timezone setting lives at the source (e.g. a filter id or 'report_settings'); surfaced verbatim to the user as lever_hint, never interpreted by core (AD-2).

tracked_entity_report.description: Story 48.5: ONE report of this source that participates in tracked-entity work, and how. Every field id named here must exist in the descriptor's own `fields` AND be selected by the named report -- a declaration that points at a field the report cannot return is a contract error, not a runtime surprise.

report_id.description: Id of a report declared in this same descriptor.

direction.description: 'observe' = the report RETURNS values that may denote a tracked entity, and nothing is requested by identity. 'collect' = the report is DRIVEN by governed source identities supplied as a request parameter; it requires identity_field_id and query_driver.

entity_kinds.description: Which kinds of entity this report can denote. Opaque to core (AD-2): the vocabulary is open so a source entity kind nobody anticipated needs no core change.

candidate_field_ids.description: Fields whose values are candidate denotations of an entity (a label, a domain, a query string). Observation evidence, never proof of a role.

identity_field_id.description: Field carrying the source's own STABLE identifier for the entity, when it has one. Required for direction='collect'.

label_field_id.description: Field carrying the human label to display beside an identifier. Presentation only.

own_marker_field_id.description: Field the source itself uses to mark a row as the connected account's own entity. Evidence for an `own` role proposal; never an automatic role.

population.description: What the observed values are a population OF. A source that omits low-volume rows for privacy still reports their totals elsewhere, so an observed candidate set is never the complete universe of entities.

completeness.description: 'declared_scope' = the report returns exactly the entities that were requested. 'reportable_subset' = the provider may withhold rows (privacy thresholds, sampling, eligibility), so absence is not evidence of absence.

note.description: Human sentence naming what is excluded, surfaced verbatim in coverage evidence.

query_driver.description: How governed source identities become a request. Required for direction='collect', forbidden for 'observe'. The core passes the resolved values through under the declared parameter name and interprets nothing about them (AD-2).

parameter.description: Keyword argument name the dispatch callable accepts.

value_source.description: Which governed value fills the parameter. Only the confirmed external identity is available today; an enum keeps a second source from arriving untyped.

cardinality.description: Drives the quota estimate: per-value multiplies the report's declared read cost by the number of bound identities.

own_marker_parameter.description: Optional second keyword argument receiving the subset of values whose Project role is `own`.

max_values_per_request.description: Provider bound on how many identities one request may carry. Null = no declared bound.

tracked_entity.description: Story 48.5: OPTIONAL, schema-versioned declaration that this source can observe or collect tracked entities (own brands, competitors, references). ABSENT means `not_applicable` with a reason -- never guessed support: core must not infer from a connector's name, nor from a field happening to be called `brand`, `advertiser`, `domain` or `keyword`. The report contracts stay the authority for grain, filters, completeness, quota, cadence, incremental behaviour and history.

tracked_entity_public.description: Story 48.5: the normalized tracked-entity answer for one project/connection. `support` is ALWAYS present, so a caller reads a reason rather than an absence: 'declared' when the connector declares one, 'not_applicable' when it declares none.
